assertion_analysis.failure_condition: assert "node-tmp-probe-write-refused" in results. Fails when the node-tmp seal is absent from fence_argv: _PROBE_STUB's touch of $FENCE_NODE_TMP_PROBE (node_tmp/probe-direct.txt, outside the scratch and the runtime paths) then succeeds and the stub records 'node-tmp-probe-write-ok'. Independently verified: negative-control-seal-removed.log shows exactly this failing line, assert 'node-tmp-probe-write-refused' in 'node-tmp-probe-write-ok' at tests/...:370, 2 failed / 6 passed, EXIT=1. This assertion is a real guard, and it closes a vacuous predecessor: at base revision 2e1f7cc4a the same file's stub touched probes only under $FENCE_OWN and the runtime paths (git show 2e1f7cc4a:tests/...:71,77), so the base's assert not (node.outside.parent / 'probe').exists() could not fail whatever the fence did.

assert seen. seen is appended by the spy installed over _worker_fence.create_write_roots and is empty unless create_node_tmp_runtime_paths calls it, so reinstating the pre-change separate creation loop reddens it. Independently verified: negative-control-runtime-paths-separate-loop.log shows AssertionError: create_node_tmp_runtime_paths did not call create_write_roots, 1 failed / 7 passed, EXIT=1. Independent of the value under test, because the spy observes the call rather than any value the test itself supplied.

assert sorted(created) == sorted(_worker_fence.resolved_destination(p) for p in roots). Reddens if create_node_tmp_runtime_paths stops returning the resolved forms of the paths it handed over (e.g. returns the unresolved inputs, or drops the second enumerate). Weak but not self-comparing: created is the function's return while the right side is re-derived from what the spy recorded, so reverting the return to unresolved paths breaks it. It is not the load-bearing assertion of this test; assert seen at :445 is.

assert argv == expected. expected is a literal list built from the fixture's own paths (node.rec, node.scratch_root, node.node_tmp, node.own, node.run, node.fleet, node.codex), while argv comes from fence_argv via node.argv(); the two sides have independent provenance, so an added, dropped or reordered mount reddens it. It pins the composed fence for a fixed root set, and monkeypatch.setattr(_worker_fence, 'shared_store_seal_roots', list) keeps the host's real delivery stores out of the expected argv.

findings.text: follow-on: both gate arms and both negative-control logs name revision ea4d59115, while the delivered head is d01e47ee1 and the done_when asks the direct-probe control to run 'at the delivered head'. The gap is one commit and it is docs-only: git diff ea4d59115 d01e47ee1 is a single file, docs/evidence/fragments/a-worker-cannot-write-your-home/the-node-tmp-seal-has-one-directory-rule.html, two changed lines of prose correcting the fragment's own revision citation (verified by reading the diff). follow-on: routing create_node_tmp_runtime_paths through create_write_roots also swaps the refusal text. The removed loop raised BackendError('cannot create the node tmp runtime path <target>, which the fence must leave writable beneath the read-only <NODE_TMP_ROOT>: <exc>'); create_write_roots (reckon/_worker_fence.py:568) raises BackendError('cannot create the write root <path>: <exc>'). A launch refused because a runtime path could not be created beneath the read-only node tmp now reports the generic write-root message and no longer names the node-tmp seal as the context the move is specific to, so an operator debugging that refusal loses the pointer to the seal. No test or call site asserts on either message (grep over reckon/ and tests/ finds the new text only at its raise site), so nothing breaks; it is a diagnostics regression of one line, not a blocking defect.
